title: Share code between the ALTREP types
description:
The C code now uses the rlang C library (`r_obj*`, `r_ssize`, `KEEP()`/`FREE()`, pointer based loops). The four ALTREP files (`altrep-sparse-double.c`, `altrep-sparse-integer.c`, `altrep-sparse-logical.c`, `altrep-sparse-string.c`) are still near copies of each other, so a fix in one has to be repeated by hand in the other three.

This issue tracks sharing that code. It builds on the rlang port, so the helpers can be written against rlang types.

## Approach

No X-macros. Use `static inline` typed helpers in a shared header (`src/sparse-altrep-common.h`), so each type keeps readable, debuggable code and the compiler can still inline.

## Tasks

- [ ] Share the callbacks that do not depend on the element type in `sparse-altrep-common.h`: `Length`, `Inspect`, `Duplicate`, `Dataptr_or_null`
- [ ] Add typed helper families (`int_`, `dbl_`, `lgl_`, `chr_`) for `Materialize`, `Extract_subset` and `Is_sorted`
- [ ] Deduplicate the remaining per type code: `Elt`, `Min`/`Max`, `Sum`, and the integer and double variants in `sparse-arithmetic.c` (multiplication)
- [ ] Compare line counts before and after
- [ ] Compare timings against the baseline below, and revert any helper where inlining costs speed

## Baseline

Measured with a vector of length 1e7 with 1e5 non-default values, median of 30 runs (`Materialize` includes building a fresh vector each run):

| Case           | Median (ms) |
| -------------- | ----------- |
| Materialize    | 34.5        |
| Extract_subset | 8           |
| multiplication | 3           |

## Constraints

- Behavior must not change. The existing tests (and snapshots for the `sparsevctrs.verbose_materialize` option) must pass unchanged.
- ALTREP callbacks keep the signatures R requires for `R_set_altrep_*_method()`.
- Follow the C conventions in `.claude/CLAUDE.md` (decl headers, `ffi_` wrappers, `clang-format`, and the explicit protection reading pass for every `r_obj*` touched).

title: Speed up `coerce_to_sparse_data_frame()`
description:
if this works, we also speed up the tibble case.

In my mind, it shouldn't take this long

``` r
library(tidymodels)
library(textrecipes)
library(friends)

preped_rec <- recipe(season ~ text, data = friends) %>%
  step_tokenize(text) %>%
  step_tf(text) %>%
  prep()
#> Warning in asMethod(object): sparse->dense coercion: allocating vector of size
#> 8.7 GiB

term_freq <- bake(preped_rec, new_data = NULL, composition = "dgCMatrix")

library(sparsevctrs)

tictoc::tic()
tmp <- coerce_to_sparse_data_frame(term_freq)
tictoc::toc()
#> 1.392 sec elapsed
```

title: using wts in sparse_var()
description:
Since we have to center `x` and multiply it with the squared weights, we will have to destroy the sparsity either way.

```r
x <- 1:10
wts <- 10:1
recipes:::wt_calcs(x, wts, "var")
#> [1] 6.875

wts <- wts / sum(wts)
center <- sum(wts * x)
x <- sqrt(wts) * (x - center)
sum(x * x) / (1 - sum(wts ^ 2))
#> [1] 6.875
```

There may be a way to do this neatly without destroying sparsity, but it isn't the biggest concern for me right now

title: fix bug in altrep_sparse_real_Dataptr()
description:
The following code should not throw an error, as setting attributes shouldn't force materialization

``` r
aaa <- 1:1000000000000

# No materialization 
attributes(aaa) <- list(h = 3)

# Forced materialization
aaa[]
#> Error: vector memory exhausted (limit reached?)
```

``` r
library(sparsevctrs)
  
options("sparsevctrs.verbose_materialize" = TRUE)
  
aaa <- new_sparse_real(1, 5, 10)

attributes(aaa) <- list(h = 3)
#> sparsevctrs: Sparse vector materialized
```

title: add way to turn normal vectors into altrep sparse vectors
Consider adding `default` property to altrep class
description:
right now there is a implicit assumption that non-specified values are zero. This doesn't have to be true, and we could include `default` as a value to `data1` and use. With this we can have `x + 1` retain its sparsity which is currently not the case.

``` r
library(sparsevctrs)

x <- new_sparse_real(c(1, 5, 10), c(1, 5, 10), 10)

x
#>  [1]  1  0  0  0  5  0  0  0  0 10

altrepr::is_altrep(x)
#> [1] TRUE

x + 1
#>  [1]  2  1  1  1  6  1  1  1  1 11

altrepr::is_altrep(x + 1)
#> [1] FALSE
```

We could also take variables that mostly take 100 as a value to become sparse with default 100

title: have threshold to materialize when subsetting down a lot
description:
I don't know if I love this idea, but it could be useful

``` r
library(sparsevctrs)

# long sparse vector
x_long <- new_sparse_real(c(1, 5, 10), c(1, 5, 10), 10000000000)

altrepr::is_altrep(x_long)
#> [1] TRUE
lobstr::obj_size(x_long)
#> 1.24 kB

# short sparse vector
x_short <- x_long[1:2]

altrepr::is_altrep(x_short)
#> [1] TRUE
lobstr::obj_size(x_short)
#> 1.21 kB

# short dense vector
x_dense <- x_short[]

altrepr::is_altrep(x_dense)
#> [1] FALSE
lobstr::obj_size(x_dense)
#> 64 B
```
